<!--
This body is where the transcript lives. A comment underneath a pull request is
not where anybody looks, so everything about the change belongs here, and a body
that turns out to be wrong or incomplete is edited rather than replied to.
-->

### What changed, and what failure it prevents

<!--
Which files, and what goes wrong today that will not go wrong once this lands.
-->

### The issue this closes

<!--
Closes #NNN. If it does not close one, name the issue it advances and say which
of that issue's done-when conditions are still open.
-->

### The means check

<!--
One sentence naming the means this artefact is made of, the language, the
format, the tool or the runtime, and the reason it fits this artefact rather
than the last one.
-->

### A limit this change made narrower

<!--
Does this change narrow something the project says it does not do, or narrow
what a check covers? If it does, name the statement that has to move and quote
the sentence that replaced it. A limit that got narrower gets a sharper
statement and never a gentler one, which is the rule at the top of
docs/what-this-project-is-not-for.md. If nothing here moves a limit, say so in
one line, because an empty section reads the same as an unasked question.
-->

### What was run

<!--
Every command behind a number or a claim above, pasted with its output, run at
the commit being pushed and against the reference the reader will have. A claim
no command can back is written as a claim and marked as one.
-->
